rows: Explore all states at depth d before d+1
Follow one path to completion before backtracking
Always move toward states that seem closer to goal
Detect biggest difference between current/goal state; find operator that reduces it
Start from goal, work toward initial state
Map structure from solved problem to new one
Whether a small well-defined space can be solved directly
Systematic search such as BFS or DFS
Exhaustive search works only when state space and operators are explicit and bounded.
Whether a large defined space needs guidance
Heuristics trade completeness for tractability unless carefully bounded.
Why an ill-defined problem feels stuck
List alternate object functions and problem framings; the obstacle may be the representation.
Why a familiar strategy keeps failing
Deliberate meta-cognitive break helps only if you try a genuinely different representation.
Whether a known analog can transfer
Spontaneous transfer is weak; map relations, not surface features.
Whether a creative leap is likely
Stepping away works after serious preparation, not instead of it.
Deliberate practice at the edge of ability
Time-on-task without feedback mostly automates current habits.
